extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, attorneys and counsel involved in USPTO disciplinary/reciprocal discipline proceedings, OED staff
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards for imposing reciprocal discipline on a registered patent practitioner under 37 C.F.R. §11.24, including notice requirements, default consequences, statutory/regulatory predicates, and publication/notification obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and opportunity to respond under 37 C.F.R. §11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must send a Notice and Order informing the respondent that a Complaint for Reciprocal Discipline has been filed and provide the respondent an opportunity to file, within forty (40) days, a response opposing the imposition of reciprocal discipline identical to that imposed by the other jurisdiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice and Order was sent by certified mail and was also published in the Official Gazette. The respondent may oppose on one or more of the reasons provided in 37 C.F.R. §11.24(d)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Default consequence of failing to respond (no genuine issue of material fact)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the respondent fails to file a response to the Notice and Order, the Office may determine there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. §11.24(d) and proceed to impose the reciprocal discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this matter, Respondent did not file a response and the Office determined reprimand was the appropriate discipline. Failure to respond can result in acceptance of the disciplinary determination from the other jurisdiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline to mirror the other jurisdiction's sanction
rubrics_metrics.description: Reciprocal discipline imposed by the USPTO is to be identical to the discipline imposed by the other jurisdiction (e.g., public reprimand), absent successful opposition under 37 C.F.R. §11.24(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Complaint requested that the USPTO impose reciprocal discipline identical to the November 15, 2019 Final Judgment and Order of the Arizona Presiding Disciplinary Judge; the Final Order here imposes the identical sanction (public reprimand).

rubrics_metrics.name: Violation predicate: 37 C.F.R. §11.804(h) (discipline for state-imposed public reprimand)
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner may be disciplined under 37 C.F.R. §11.804(h) when there is a public reprimand on ethical grounds by a duly constituted authority of a State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This Final Order states Respondent is publicly reprimanded by the USPTO for violation of 37 C.F.R. §11.804(h), predicated upon the Arizona public reprimand.

rubrics_metrics.name: State professional conduct violations as predicates for USPTO discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Ethical violations found by the state (here Arizona Rule 42, ERs 1.2, 1.3, 1.4, 1.5, and 1.7) can serve as the factual/legal predicate for USPTO discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this case the Arizona public reprimand was predicated on failing to perform legal services required by his client and failing to obtain informed consent to a conflict of interest during preparation of a non-provisional patent application; such state findings support USPTO reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory and regulatory authority for discipline and publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplinary actions and the imposition of reciprocal discipline are taken pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §32 and 37 C.F.R. §11.24.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order expressly cites 35 U.S.C. §32 and 37 C.F.R. §11.24 as the bases for the reprimand and the publication requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and notification obligations (Official Gazette, FOIA, notice to jurisdictions) under 37 C.F.R. §11.59
rubrics_metrics.description: When public discipline is imposed, the OED Director must publish a Notice of Public Reprimand in the Official Gazette, make disciplinary decisions available for public review (OED FOIA Reading Room), and give notice pursuant to 37 C.F.R. §11.59 to state disciplinary agencies, courts where the respondent is admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order directs publication of the Notice in the Official Gazette, cites the FOIA Reading Room URL for public review, and directs notice to disciplinary enforcement agencies and courts where Respondent is admitted.
